features.name: Surface polish
features.description: This captures how error-free and professionally proofread the letter is at the sentence level.

levels.descriptor: Frequent typos, misspellings, or broken wording distract from the content and noticeably reduce professionalism.
Noticeable errors recur, but the letter remains understandable overall.
Only minor isolated errors appear, and the letter reads mostly polished.
The letter is essentially error-free and feels carefully proofread.

features.evidence: Strong command of data structures and algorithms
features.name: Narrative cohesion
features.description: This captures whether the letter reads as a connected case for candidacy rather than a stack of disconnected claims.

levels.descriptor: The letter feels disjointed, fragment-heavy, or checklist-like, with little sense of progression.
The letter has a basic structure, but transitions are weak and sections still feel stitched together.
The letter shows a clear progression from motivation to evidence to fit, with mostly coherent flow.
The letter builds a strong through-line that integrates motivation, experience, and role match into one persuasive story.

features.name: Targeting precision
features.description: This captures how specifically the letter maps the applicant's background to this exact Google security engineering role rather than to security work in general.

levels.descriptor: The letter could fit almost any software or security application, with little reference to this team's specific work.
The letter shows some role interest but only lightly echoes the posting.
The letter references several job-specific elements such as AI agents, vulnerability handling, variant analysis, or collaboration with security engineers.
The letter tightly maps past work to the posting's exact charter and shows a tailored understanding of the team.

features.evidence: too many signals, too few experts
features.name: Scaling thesis
features.description: This captures whether the applicant articulates the core problem of scaling scarce security expertise through automation and tooling.

levels.descriptor: The letter does not present a clear view of how security tooling scales expert work.
The letter shows general interest in security automation without a sharp problem framing.
The letter clearly frames automation as a way to reduce repetitive security toil or expand team capacity.
The letter presents a sophisticated scaling view, such as multiplying scarce judgment through triage systems, variant analysis, or fleet-wide leverage.

features.evidence: improvements there are inherited by every team downstream
features.name: Leverage orientation
features.description: This captures how strongly the letter values foundation-level work whose effects propagate across many teams or products.

levels.descriptor: Motivation is framed mostly as interest in the job itself, not in platform-level leverage.
The letter mentions scale or broad impact briefly but does not dwell on it.
The letter clearly values foundational or internal platform work because it benefits many teams or products.
The letter repeatedly frames past choices and future goals around downstream leverage across an organization.

features.evidence: make the secure path the easy path
features.name: Enablement mindset
features.description: This captures whether the applicant frames security as helping developers succeed through defaults and tools rather than through process alone.

levels.descriptor: The letter does not frame security work in terms of helping developers.
The letter mentions helping teams in general terms without a concrete enablement stance.
The letter clearly emphasizes making secure practices easier or more routine for engineers.
The letter strongly presents security as developer enablement through low-friction defaults, tooling, and assistance rather than policing.

features.name: Production scope
features.description: This captures the amount of real production delivery experience the letter claims in testing, maintaining, operating, and launching software systems.

levels.descriptor: The letter shows only minimum-qualifying experience or limited production launch ownership, typically around 2 to 3 years and few services.
The letter shows solid early-career production work with some testing, maintenance, and launch ownership.
The letter shows substantial production scope, typically around 5 years or repeated ownership across several services.
The letter shows extensive production scope with long tenure and broad multi-service responsibility, often 7 or more years or many launches.

features.name: Academic attainment
features.description: This captures the highest formal education level claimed, which varies directly with a stated preferred qualification.

levels.descriptor: Bachelor's degree or equivalent only, with no advanced degree claimed.
Master's degree claimed.
Doctoral degree or comparable research doctorate claimed.

features.name: Go centrality
features.description: This captures how central Go appears to the applicant's real production work rather than merely being one language they know.

levels.descriptor: Go is only briefly mentioned or not tied to meaningful ownership.
Go appears in recent work but not as a dominant language.
Go is clearly a main language for backend or service work.
Go is framed as the primary or daily-driver language with substantial system ownership.

features.name: Python ownership
features.description: This captures the depth and production seriousness of the applicant's Python work for services, tooling, or automation.

levels.descriptor: Python is absent or mentioned only in passing.
Python appears for scripts or general tooling without much depth.
Python is clearly used for production automation, services, or internal tools.
Python is presented as a major production language with maintainable services or tooling that others rely on.

features.name: Agentic architecture
features.description: This captures whether the letter shows design ownership of agentic systems, especially bounded Python agents supervised by Go infrastructure.

levels.descriptor: No agentic or agent-based systems experience is described.
Agents are mentioned at a high level without concrete architecture or control details.
The letter describes designing agentic systems with a clear division between agents and supporting services.
The letter shows end-to-end ownership of constrained agentic architecture, emphasizing permissions, guardrails, auditability, or explicit contracts.

features.name: AI reliability
features.description: This captures how concretely the letter shows production AI experience with attention to evaluation, failure modes, or trustworthiness.

levels.descriptor: No applied AI work is described.
AI is mentioned as exposure or experimentation without production evidence.
The letter claims production delivery of model-backed or LLM-based features.
The letter pairs production AI work with explicit attention to evaluation, failure modes, guardrails, or trustworthiness.

features.name: Triage automation
features.description: This captures direct experience automating vulnerability intake, classification, deduplication, routing, or related response workflows.

levels.descriptor: No concrete vulnerability-handling automation is described.
The letter expresses interest in reducing manual security work but gives no delivered example.
The letter describes building automation for vulnerability intake or triage.
The letter shows substantive ownership of a pipeline for classification, routing, deduplication, or similar workflow mechanics, often with clear operational effect.

features.evidence: mapping attack surfaces and validating fixes
features.name: Assessment practice
features.description: This captures the depth of hands-on security review work the applicant describes, from checklists to substantive analysis and fix validation.

levels.descriptor: No security assessment work is mentioned.
Security reviews are mentioned vaguely or as a light supporting activity.
The letter names concrete practices such as threat modeling, design review, or targeted component review.
The letter shows hands-on structured assessment work with attack-surface reasoning, verification of fixes, or deep review responsibility.

features.evidence: turned a brute-force correlation job into a streaming computation
features.name: Algorithmic fluency
features.description: This captures how convincingly the letter shows applied data-structures-and-algorithms skill on real engineering problems.

levels.descriptor: The letter does not provide evidence of algorithmic skill.
The letter claims strength in data structures or algorithms but offers no concrete example.
The letter gives a concrete example of using an algorithmic idea or data structure to improve a system.
The letter gives a strong example in which algorithmic redesign materially improved performance, scalability, or tractability.

features.evidence: hours of expert attention it returned
features.name: Outcome specificity
features.description: This captures whether the letter backs claims with observable results rather than only naming activities.

levels.descriptor: Most claims stay at the level of responsibilities or adjectives, with no stated results.
Some benefits are implied, but outcomes remain vague.
The letter links projects to concrete qualitative results such as reduced toil or improved tractability.
The letter gives quantified results or especially crisp operational outcomes that make the impact easy to visualize.

features.name: Security credential
features.description: This captures whether the letter includes an externally recognized security certification and how demanding it appears.

levels.descriptor: No external security certification is mentioned.
A baseline certification such as Security+ is mentioned.
A demanding hands-on certification such as OSCP or stronger is mentioned.

features.name: Offensive practice
features.description: This captures ongoing adversarial security practice outside normal development work, especially through capture-the-flag events or similar exercises.

levels.descriptor: No adversarial practice outside normal work is mentioned.
The letter mentions occasional participation or casual practice without depth signals.
The letter shows regular or serious engagement in adversarial exercises.
The letter shows unusually strong external practice, such as near-top finishes or another high-commitment signal.

features.evidence: maintain an open-source framework with users
features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: This captures whether the applicant merely contributes fixes upstream or actually owns a project that others rely on.

levels.descriptor: No open-source contribution is mentioned.
The letter mentions occasional upstream patches or small contributions.
The letter claims a maintainer role for a project or library.
The letter shows stewardship of a project with external users or contributors, including reviews, releases, or roadmap ownership.

features.evidence: distributed key-value store with replication and failure recovery
features.name: Project ambition
features.description: This captures the technical ambition of the applicant's self-driven projects, especially whether they tackle hard systems problems rather than only small utilities.

levels.descriptor: No self-driven technical project is mentioned.
The letter mentions only a small utility or simple app with limited technical stretch.
The letter describes a meaningful personal project with some systems, reliability, or implementation depth.
The letter describes an ambitious project that tackles hard systems problems such as storage, replication, consensus, scheduling, or failure recovery.
